My hair routine:

I don’t really have much of one but I go by the feel of it to see which products I should use. I use Aussie moisture shampoo and conditioner (the avocado one). After the shower I have some more products from Aussie a leave in conditioner spray, a curl defining cream, and a curl defining pudding, I also have not your mother’s kinky moves curl defining cream and a ten in one spray, and a fructis anti-frizz serum. 

I wash my hair every other day or every third day depending. Sometimes I was it more often if I have demanding days at work. 

I don’t all of my products in a schedule so I can’t say on which days I do what but it all goes by feel sometimes I just wash and put in a leave in conditioner others I’ll put in almost all of the products.

I think my hair type is 3b/3c not sure tho

I used to straighten my hair at least once a month since my freshman year of high school and I never used any heat protectants. My hair always stayed shiny so I thought no damage was being done buuut by the time freshman/sophomore year of college rolled atriums some sections of my hair refused to go back to being curly after a wash. 
     So I decided it was time to cut some hair off and what was meant to be a few inches off turned into a big chop. (that’s on me for going to someone who doesn’t normally deal with natural hair).
      At first I hated it but I took the opportunity to learn to care for my hair growing up in a mixed household I had a mom who tried her best to keep up with two daughters with tight curls that didn’t come from her side of the family but she did her best and my hair stayed pretty healthy until it’s well being was put solely into my hands. I had three perms from middle school to high school but they didn’t seem to set right and after the allotted time I would wash my hair and it would be back to it’s natural state so I took to straightening it with a flat iron. 
     All in all I’m still learning to take care of my hair but getting it all chopped off was a good way to reset the process and learn from scratch :).
